body:
I merged `upstream/main` into this branch (merge commit d7982d620). This is a merge with hand edits, so it needs a review of the merge commit.

What the merge changed:

- Upstream #2566 split `tool_import.rs` into `tool_import/mod.rs` and `tool_import/report.rs`. This branch made the same split as `tool_import_report.rs`. The merge keeps the upstream layout and removes `tool_import_report.rs`.
- This branch changes `tool_numbers::numbers` to return a `Result`. Upstream added two new callers. The merge updates them:
  - `crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/mod.rs`: `.map_err(CommandError::Invalid)?`.
  - `crates/app/src/tool_table.rs`: `?` (the function already returns `Result<String, String>`).
- The gate map line in `crates/app/tests/tool_import_modes.rs` no longer names `tool_import_report`.

Readings on head d7982d620:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 261 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy lanes (#2568): not run. The diff reaches 185 `app heavy` steps. I will run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base main` before the PR is flagged ready.

The PR stays a draft. It is ready for a re-check.

The heavy lanes ran on head d7982d620 (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`, #2568): 185 steps, 0 failed. The PR body now has the readings on the final head, and it says that the `tool_import` split now comes from upstream #2566. The branch merges cleanly with `upstream/main` at c4ac3ce6d. I flag the PR ready for review.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d7982d620655cd5413913ce777fa639f98406c6d -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Review tier: safety. The PR changes the T/H number law of the post. A tool with no number and no free number now gives a refusal. Before, it posted as `T4294967295`.

## What looks good

- All four items of #2517 are done:
  1. `crates/app/tests/tool_numbers.rs` has 354 lines, and `tool_numbers/stable.rs` has 247 lines. The `tool_import` split comes from upstream #2566. The `#[test]` count goes from 10 to 13. No test is removed.
  2. There are two new legacy-load tests: one with a document order that is not the name order, and one with numbered and unnumbered tools in the same file.
  3. The `u32::MAX` fallback is removed. `tool_numbers::assign` gives a refusal that names the tool. `numbers` returns `Result`. The post, `ImportTools` and `tool_table::export` propagate the refusal. `clash` returns it as a refusal. `number_of` and `next_free` read it as `None`.
  4. The dead `None => "number cleared"` arm is removed. `SetToolNumber::number()` gives the status text.
- The code adds no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`.
- The comment over the T/H law in `posting.rs` now agrees with the code.
- The PR changes no `.nc` or `.cl` golden file. No golden moves.
- The hand edits of merge commit d7982d620 (remerge-diff) are correct. They keep the upstream layout of `tool_import/`, remove this branch's `tool_import_report.rs`, and move the fallible `numbers` call into the two new callers. The final diff against main has no other change in `tool_import`.

## Results, merged with main

Built locally (macOS) on a trial merge of d7982d620 with `upstream/main` 06d349391. The merge is clean.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 261 steps, 0 failed. This includes:
  - `app suites: tool_numbers`
  - `app suites: tool_import_modes`, `tool_library`, `tool_library_holders`, `tool_table`
  - `ui suites: lib`
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`, release, `--ignored`): 185 steps, 0 failed. The lanes are each `app heavy:` binary and `app heavy: doc`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The `drop_non_drop` error that the PR body names is not on the current main.

Mutations (each one reverted after its run):

- I put back `next_free_from(&taken).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)` in `assign`. Then `an_unnumbered_tool_with_no_free_number_is_refused_by_name` fails (red).
- I removed the name sort in `freeze_legacy_tool_numbers` (`project/apply.rs`). Then `stable::a_legacy_project_numbers_by_name_order_not_by_document_order` fails with `first by name: left Some(2), right Some(1)` (red). This is the same result as in the PR body.
- With the code of the PR, the two tests pass (green).

Extra suites run: none were necessary. The diff changes no file under `testdata/` and no import code.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: the status text is the same as before (`tool <name> is now T<n>`). The PR has no visible UI change, so it needs no screenshots.
- `clash` refuses when any tool of the document has no number and none is free, also when the program does not use that tool. This is safe, and the doc comment says so. Only a file with 99999 numbered tools can show this.
- Not from this PR: `freeze_legacy_tool_numbers` (`crates/app/src/project/apply.rs:999`) still has `unwrap_or(u32::MAX)` for the list position. Also, a legacy position can be equal to a number that a different tool carries. The clash law then refuses the post by name, so the output is not wrong.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
